subject.title: fix(line): cap message action text length

question: Should LINE message actions with text beyond LINE’s 300-grapheme limit be centrally truncated to a deliverable action, rather than rejected or redesigned as mapped/postback commands?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow and evidence-backed, but choosing what an over-limit user tap means is a channel compatibility policy that tests cannot settle.

options.title: Accept centralized truncation
options.body: Merge the PR so invalid over-limit message actions become deliverable actions whose emitted text is the first 300 grapheme clusters.

options.title: Require an overflow failure
options.body: Pause this PR and define an upstream-visible error path so callers must shorten or redesign over-limit action text.

options.title: Use mapped command identifiers
options.body: Pause for a broader owner design that maps long structured commands to bounded action values such as postback data.

recommendation.title: Accept centralized truncation
recommendation.body: Merge the PR so invalid over-limit message actions become deliverable actions whose emitted text is the first 300 grapheme clusters.

likelyOwner.reason: VectorPeak has supplied the implementation rationale and live LINE evidence, though a current-main LINE-area owner should make the final product choice.
